filename: Differentiable modeling to unify machine learning and physical models and advance Geosciences_.pdf
title: Differentiable modeling to unify machine learning and physical models and advance Geosciences
parameterization_target: Hydrologic model parameters, runoff mechanisms, soil hydraulic properties, Manning's roughness coefficient, photosynthesis parameters
testbed_rationale: This paper is a review/perspective article summarizing differentiable modeling paradigms and reviewing existing literature, rather than releasing a new benchmark dataset or model code repository.
pain_points: Reimplementation cost for legacy models into automatic differentiation frameworks
Vanishing/exploding gradient problems when differentiating through long time-stepping numerical solvers
Mathematical non-differentiabilities (e.g. thresholds, conditional branching) requiring continuous approximations
Severe data scarcity, heterogeneity, and spatial/temporal imbalances across geoscientific domains
Nonstationarity under climate change causing out-of-distribution generalization failures
Equifinality and non-uniqueness in physical parameter inversion
extraction_notes: This is a Perspective paper published in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment. It reviews differentiable geosciences (DG) / differentiable parameter learning (dPL) and highlights case studies from prior work (e.g., Feng et al., 2022; Tsai et al., 2021).
